rv.q: A trio of captivating artists—Lisette Oropesa, Rosa Feola, and Ermonela Jaho—alternate in the touchstone soprano role of Violetta Valéry, the ill-fated Parisian courtesan fighting for love before her time runs out. Tony Award–winning director Michael Mayer conjures a dreamy setting that matches the poetry and passion of the unforgettable score.
With carefully shaded line readings and nuanced singing, she makes it sound like she's spent lots of time with the score so she could emulate the emotions of the heroine, both shown and implied.
In all, this was Oropesa and Salsi's evening and one more win for the 2025-26 Metropolitan Opera season.
His attention to dynamics enlivened the vibrant, supple carpet of orchestral sound, an important factor in making this performance so moving.
This binge resulted in experiencing two very satisfying portrayals of one of opera’s most iconic characters.
This production is certainly for someone.

cn.t: Critics praise this Met revival of Verdi's tragedy, highlighting captivating performances from the three Violettas—Oropesa, Feola, and Jaho—and Michael Mayer's visually stunning production with its jewel-toned costumes and dreamy aesthetic.
